hints.title: Determining Protocol Family from Delimiter
hints.text: Examine delimiters: an IPv4 address has exactly three periods separating four chunks, while IPv6 has exactly seven colons separating eight chunks.

hints.title: Verifying Chunk Syntax and Boundaries
hints.text: For IPv4, each chunk must be 1 to 3 digits without leading zeros in range 0 to 255. For IPv6, each chunk must be 1 to 4 hexadecimal characters.

hints.title: Granular Token Parsing and Validation
hints.text: Check if string contains period or colon. If period, split into 4 parts, verifying digits only, no leading zeros, and value between 0 and 255. If colon, split into 8 parts, verifying 1 to 4 valid hex characters.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal linear O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space validating IP token formats.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard integer parsing functions accept leading signs or whitespace which violate protocol standards.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Explicit string token validation avoids compiling complex regular expressions.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle edge cases like trailing delimiters, leading zeros, and non-hexadecimal symbols.
